about: The demo state of /architect: two fictional workspaces. Everything here is invented; no real company, person or model is described. `anaplan-architect demo --data DATA` (or Reset the demo in Settings) writes exactly this, replacing any earlier copy.

edges.reason: Import from Caldergate FP&A - Assumptions into Inputs - Settings has not run since August 2022; HR analytics key the NI and pension rates by hand each year instead.

documents.summary: The implementation partner's design record for Caldergate FP&A: naming, time and versions, volumes, revenue, the opex forecast logic, FX, margin, the P&L by cost centre, depreciation, the packs, and the open items, each with the reason for the decision.

Monthly notes of the planning systems steering meeting for 2023: the Treasury FX file stopping and the fixed 1.27 rate, the Budget v2 re-cut that was never approved, and the product master falling out of date.

The second partner's handover of Workforce Planning: its own naming, the manual steps, why the NI constants sit beside the salaries in INP03 Headcount, the feed into FP&A, and the Hub v1 import left behind.
A change request to add a thirteenth branch to Forecast Opex for legal fees. Open. It records that moving the mapping to a lookup module is agreed in principle and out of scope.
A change request to delete CAL05 Opex OLD, replaced by CAL03 Opex in 2021. Deferred until the FY22 audit file is closed, because the auditors' working papers reference its numbers.

The script behind the Data Hub's Daily Load: it pulls general ledger transactions from NetSuite, maps the source system codes and writes the import file. Its docstrings say why Source System is held as text.

questions.text: Why is the account mapping written into the Forecast Opex formula instead of a lookup table?
Why is the margin module called CAL04 Margn?

Give me an overview of the build.

How many line items use FINDITEM, and which modules are they in?
